9:1.sourceText: Καὶ παράγων εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον τυφλὸν ἐκ γενετῆς.
9:1.targetText: And passing by, He saw a man blind from birth,

9:2.sourceText: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Ῥαββεί, τίς ἥμαρτεν, οὗτος ἢ οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἵνα τυφλὸς γεννηθῇ;
9:2.targetText: and His disciples asked Him, saying, “Rabbi, who sinned, this one or his parents, that he should be born blind?”

9:3.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Οὔτε οὗτος ἥμαρτεν οὔτε οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ’ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ.
9:3.targetText: Jesus answered, “Neither this one sinned nor his parents, but that the works of God may be revealed in him;

9:4.sourceText: ἡμᾶς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ πέμψαντός με ἕως ἡμέρα ἐστίν· ἔρχεται νὺξ ὅτε οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐργάζεσθαι.
9:4.targetText: it is necessary for Me to be working the works of Him who sent Me while it is day; night comes when no one is able to work:

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness/person difference: N1904 ἡμᾶς means us; LSV Me follows the singular ἐμέ reading. First-person plural and singular subjects are not equated.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness/person difference: LSV names Me as the worker; N1904 has the plural accusative subject ἡμᾶς (us).

9:5.sourceText: ὅταν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ὦ, φῶς εἰμι τοῦ κόσμου.
9:5.targetText: when I am in the world, I AM [the] light of the world.”

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV supplies a bracketed article before light; N1904 φῶς is anarthrous.

9:6.sourceText: ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἔπτυσεν χαμαὶ καὶ ἐποίησεν πηλὸν ἐκ τοῦ πτύσματος, καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτοῦ τὸν πηλὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς,
9:6.targetText: Saying these things, He spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and rubbed the clay on the eyes of the blind man, and said to him,

groups.note: N1904 ἐπέθηκεν means put/applied on, while LSV rubbed follows the smearing verb ἐπέχρισεν reading. Both describe applying clay to the eyes; the contextual action correspondence does not assert identical Greek lexemes.

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness/explicit referent difference: N1904 αὐτοῦ is a possessive his qualifying the eyes; LSV names the blind man instead, using a different noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness/explicit referent difference: LSV identifies the eye-owner as the blind man; N1904 has the possessive αὐτοῦ without a blind adjective or man noun in this phrase.

9:7.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὕπαγε νίψαι εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν τοῦ Σιλωάμ (ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Ἀπεσταλμένος). ἀπῆλθεν οὖν καὶ ἐνίψατο, καὶ ἦλθεν βλέπων.
9:7.targetText: “Go away, wash at the pool of Siloam,” which is, interpreted, Sent. He went away, therefore, and washed, and came seeing;

sourceMoved.reason: The and said to him clause from raw Greek9:7 is rendered and exactly linked at the end of LSV9:6.

9:8.sourceText: Οἱ οὖν γείτονες καὶ οἱ θεωροῦντες αὐτὸν τὸ πρότερον, ὅτι προσαίτης ἦν, ἔλεγον Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ καθήμενος καὶ προσαιτῶν;
9:8.targetText: the neighbors, therefore, and those seeing him before, that he was blind, said, “Is this not he who is sitting and begging?”

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness difference: N1904 προσαίτης means beggar; LSV blind follows the τυφλός reading. The different descriptors are not treated as lexical equivalents.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV says he was blind; N1904 says he was a beggar, προσαίτης.

9:9.sourceText: ἄλλοι ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν· ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Οὐχί, ἀλλὰ ὅμοιος αὐτῷ ἐστιν. ἐκεῖνος ἔλεγεν ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι.
9:9.targetText: Others said, “This is he”; and others, “He is like to him”; he himself said, “I am [he].”

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the first quotation; LSV uses direct speech with no separate that.
English ellipsis: N1904 repeats said with the second others; LSV leaves that second saying verb unexpressed.
Source witness/wording difference: N1904 explicitly has Οὐχί, ἀλλά (No, but); LSV’s second opinion starts directly He is like to him.
Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the man’s direct self-identification; LSV has no separate that.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness/coordination difference: LSV explicitly joins the second others with and; N1904 begins ἄλλοι without a conjunction.
Translation addition: LSV supplies a bracketed predicate pronoun in I am; N1904 has only Ἐγώ εἰμι.

9:10.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ Πῶς οὖν ἠνεῴχθησάν σου οἱ ὀφθαλμοί;
9:10.targetText: They said, therefore, to him, “How were your eyes opened?”

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness/wording difference: N1904 repeats οὖν (then) after How; LSV does not separately render this second connective.

9:11.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος Ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰησοῦς πηλὸν ἐποίησεν καὶ ἐπέχρισέν μου τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ εἶπέν μοι ὅτι Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν Σιλωὰμ καὶ νίψαι· ἀπελθὼν οὖν καὶ νιψάμενος ἀνέβλεψα.
9:11.targetText: He answered and said, “A man called Jesus made clay, and rubbed my eyes, and said to me, Go away to the pool of Siloam, and wash; and having gone away and having washed, I received sight”;

groups.note: N1904 οὖν is then/therefore in the narrative transition; LSV renders that transition with and. This does not claim identical discourse force.

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the quoted instruction; LSV uses direct speech without that.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV adds and said immediately after He answered; N1904 ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος proceeds directly into the answer.
Source witness/explicit place-description difference: LSV names the pool of Siloam; N1904 simply names Siloam after the article, without a pool noun in this phrase.

9:12.sourceText: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ποῦ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος; λέγει Οὐκ οἶδα.
9:12.targetText: they said, therefore, to him, “Where is that One?” He says, “I have not known.”

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness/connective difference: N1904 begins καί (and); LSV uses therefore in this transition instead.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness/connective difference: LSV has inferential therefore, while pinned N1904 has additive καί (and).

9:13.sourceText: Ἄγουσιν αὐτὸν πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους, τόν ποτε τυφλόν.
9:13.targetText: They bring him who once [was] blind to the Pharisees,

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV supplies a bracketed copula in the substantival blind-person phrase; N1904 has no finite copula there.

9:14.sourceText: ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ τὸν πηλὸν ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἀνέῳξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς.
9:14.targetText: and it was a Sabbath when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.

9:15.sourceText: πάλιν οὖν ἠρώτων αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πῶς ἀνέβλεψεν. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πηλὸν ἐπέθηκέν μου ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς, καὶ ἐνιψάμην, καὶ βλέπω.
9:15.targetText: Again, therefore, the Pharisees also were asking him how he received sight, and he said to them, “He put clay on my eyes, and I washed—and I see.”

9:16.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων τινές Οὐκ ἔστιν οὗτος παρὰ Θεοῦ ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὅτι τὸ σάββατον οὐ τηρεῖ. ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Πῶς δύναται ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλὸς τοιαῦτα σημεῖα ποιεῖν; καὶ σχίσμα ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς.
9:16.targetText: Certain of the Pharisees therefore said, “This Man is not from God, because He does not keep the Sabbath”; others said, “How is a man—a sinful one—able to do such signs?” And there was a division among them.

9:17.sourceText: λέγουσιν οὖν τῷ τυφλῷ πάλιν Τί σὺ λέγεις περὶ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν ὅτι Προφήτης ἐστίν.
9:17.targetText: They said to the blind man again, “You—what do you say of Him—that He opened your eyes?”

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness/wording difference: N1904 οὖν (then/therefore) has no separate rendering in the LSV introductory sentence.
Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the quoted He is a prophet statement, which LSV places in the next verse; no separate that is rendered.

sourceMoved.reason: The answer And he said, He is a prophet is rendered in LSV9:18 and linked there to these raw Greek9:17 tokens. The separate quotation-introducing ὅτι is explained as unexpressed.

9:18.sourceText: οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἦν τυφλὸς καὶ ἀνέβλεψεν, ἕως ὅτου ἐφώνησαν τοὺς γονεῖς αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἀναβλέψαντος
9:18.targetText: And he said, “He is a prophet.” The Jews, therefore, did not believe concerning him that he was blind and received sight, until they called the parents of him who received sight,

9:19.sourceText: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτοὺς λέγοντες Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ὑμῶν, ὃν ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη; πῶς οὖν βλέπει ἄρτι;
9:19.targetText: and they asked them, saying, “Is [this] your son, of whom you say that he was born blind? How then does he now see?”

9:20.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπαν Οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ἡμῶν καὶ ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη·
9:20.targetText: His parents answered them and said, “We have known that this is our son, and that he was born blind;

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness/wording difference: N1904 οὖν (then/therefore) has no separate counterpart in the LSV introduction.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness/explicit recipient difference: LSV adds them after answered; pinned N1904 has no corresponding object pronoun there.

9:21.sourceText: πῶς δὲ νῦν βλέπει οὐκ οἴδαμεν, ἢ τίς ἤνοιξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἡμεῖς οὐκ οἴδαμεν· αὐτὸν ἐρωτήσατε, ἡλικίαν ἔχει, αὐτὸς περὶ ἑαυτοῦ λαλήσει.
9:21.targetText: and how he now sees, we have not known; or who opened his eyes, we have not known; he is of age, ask him; he himself will speak concerning himself.”

groups.note: Greek has age expresses adulthood; LSV renders the complete idiom as he is of age, not a general lexical equivalence of have and be.

9:22.sourceText: ταῦτα εἶπαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐφοβοῦντο τοὺς Ἰουδαίους· ἤδη γὰρ συνετέθειντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἵνα ἐάν τις αὐτὸν ὁμολογήσῃ Χριστόν, ἀποσυνάγωγος γένηται.
9:22.targetText: His parents said these things, because they were afraid of the Jews, for the Jews had already agreed together, that if anyone may confess Him—Christ, he may be put out of the synagogue;

targetPhrases.text: he may be put out of the synagogue

9:23.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπαν ὅτι Ἡλικίαν ἔχει, αὐτὸν ἐπερωτήσατε.
9:23.targetText: because of this his parents said, “He is of age, ask him.”

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the parents quotation; LSV uses direct speech with no separate that.

9:24.sourceText: Ἐφώνησαν οὖν τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐκ δευτέρου ὃς ἦν τυφλὸς, καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Δὸς δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ· ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.
9:24.targetText: They called, therefore, the man who was blind a second time, and they said to him, “Give glory to God, we have known that this Man is a sinner”;

9:25.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη οὖν ἐκεῖνος Εἰ ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν οὐκ οἶδα· ἓν οἶδα, ὅτι τυφλὸς ὢν ἄρτι βλέπω.
9:25.targetText: he answered, therefore, and said, “If He is a sinner—I have not known, one thing I have known, that, being blind, now I see.”

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV includes and said after answered; N1904 proceeds directly from ἀπεκρίθη οὖν ἐκεῖνος into the reply.

9:26.sourceText: εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ Τί ἐποίησέν σοι; πῶς ἤνοιξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς;
9:26.targetText: And they said to him again, “What did He do to you? How did He open your eyes?”

groups.note: N1904 has continuative οὖν (then/therefore), while LSV introduces the question with And. The transition is linked contextually without asserting identical connective force.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV repeats again with the question; N1904 has no πάλιν qualifier in this verse.

9:27.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς Εἶπον ὑμῖν ἤδη καὶ οὐκ ἠκούσατε· τί πάλιν θέλετε ἀκούειν; μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε αὐτοῦ μαθηταὶ γενέσθαι;
9:27.targetText: He answered them, “I told you already, and you did not hear; why do you wish to hear [it] again? Do you also wish to become His disciples?”

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή marks negative expectation in the discipleship question; LSV Do you also wish has no separately expressed negative particle.

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV supplies a bracketed object for hear; N1904 has no object pronoun in that infinitive phrase.

9:28.sourceText: καὶ ἐλοιδόρησαν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπαν Σὺ μαθητὴς εἶ ἐκείνου, ἡμεῖς δὲ τοῦ Μωϋσέως ἐσμὲν μαθηταί·
9:28.targetText: They reviled him, therefore, and said, “You are His disciple, and we are Moses’ disciples;

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness connective difference: N1904 begins καί (and); LSV instead has therefore in the introduction.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness connective difference: LSV uses inferential therefore, while N1904 has an initial additive καί.

9:29.sourceText: ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι Μωϋσεῖ λελάληκεν ὁ Θεός, τοῦτον δὲ οὐκ οἴδαμεν πόθεν ἐστίν.
9:29.targetText: we have known that God has spoken to Moses, but this One—we have not known where He is from.”

9:30.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐν τούτῳ γὰρ τὸ θαυμαστόν ἐστιν, ὅτι ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε πόθεν ἐστίν, καὶ ἤνοιξέν μου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς.
9:30.targetText: The man answered and said to them, “Why, in this is a wonderful thing, that you have not known where He is from, and He opened my eyes!

groups.note: The LSV interjection Why frames in this as a rhetorical response to ἐν τούτῳ γάρ (for in this). The full discourse frame is paired; γάρ alone is not assigned the lexical interrogative meaning why.

9:31.sourceText: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἀκούει, ἀλλ’ ἐάν τις θεοσεβὴς ᾖ καὶ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιῇ, τούτου ἀκούει.
9:31.targetText: And we have known that God does not hear sinners, but if anyone may be a worshiper of God, and may do His will, He hears him;

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV begins And; N1904 begins directly οἴδαμεν without a connective.

9:32.sourceText: ἐκ τοῦ αἰῶνος οὐκ ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν τις ὀφθαλμοὺς τυφλοῦ γεγεννημένου·
9:32.targetText: from the age it was not heard that anyone opened eyes of one who has been born blind;

9:33.sourceText: εἰ μὴ ἦν οὗτος παρὰ Θεοῦ, οὐκ ἠδύνατο ποιεῖν οὐδέν.
9:33.targetText: if this One were not from God, He were not able to do anything.”

9:34.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἐν ἁμαρτίαις σὺ ἐγεννήθης ὅλος, καὶ σὺ διδάσκεις ἡμᾶς; καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω.
9:34.targetText: They answered and said to him, “In sins you were born altogether, and you teach us?” And they cast him forth outside.

9:35.sourceText: Ἤκουσεν Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω, καὶ εὑρὼν αὐτὸν εἶπεν Σὺ πιστεύεις εἰς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;
9:35.targetText: Jesus heard that they cast him forth outside, and having found him, He said to him, “Do you believe in the Son of God?”

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness title difference: N1904 has τοῦ ἀνθρώπου (of Man); LSV has of God, following the alternative Θεοῦ reading. The two nouns are not treated as lexical equivalents.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness/explicit recipient difference: LSV adds to him after said; N1904 has no separate recipient pronoun there.
Source witness title difference: LSV names God where pinned N1904 has of Man.

9:36.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν Καὶ τίς ἐστιν, Κύριε, ἵνα πιστεύσω εἰς αὐτόν;
9:36.targetText: He answered and said, “Who is He, Lord, that I may believe in Him?”

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness/wording difference: N1904 opens the quoted question with Καί (and); LSV begins directly Who is He.

9:37.sourceText: εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Καὶ ἑώρακας αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετὰ σοῦ ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν.
9:37.targetText: And Jesus said to him, “You have both seen Him, and He who is speaking with you is He”;

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV introduces the answer with And; N1904 begins directly εἶπεν without a conjunction.

9:38.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἔφη Πιστεύω, Κύριε· καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτῷ.
9:38.targetText: and he said, “I believe, Lord,” and worshiped Him.

9:39.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰς κρίμα ἐγὼ εἰς τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον ἦλθον, ἵνα οἱ μὴ βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ οἱ βλέποντες τυφλοὶ γένωνται.
9:39.targetText: And Jesus said, “I came to this world for judgment, that those not seeing may see, and those seeing may become blind.”

9:40.sourceText: ἤκουσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων ταῦτα οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες, καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Μὴ καὶ ἡμεῖς τυφλοί ἐσμεν;
9:40.targetText: And those of the Pharisees who were with Him heard these things, and they said to Him, “Are we also blind?”

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή marks negative expectation; LSV Are we also blind has no separately expressed negative particle.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV begins And; N1904 has no initial connective in this verse.

9:41.sourceText: εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ τυφλοὶ ἦτε, οὐκ ἂν εἴχετε ἁμαρτίαν· νῦν δὲ λέγετε ὅτι Βλέπομεν· ἡ ἁμαρτία ὑμῶν μένει.
9:41.targetText: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you were not having had sin, but now you say—We see, therefore your sin remains.”

groups.note: Greek οὐκ ἂν εἴχετε is the negative modal imperfect have construction (would not have); LSV prints the expanded you were not having had. The contextual have meaning is linked without asserting identical English tense/aspect.

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces We see; LSV gives direct speech without a separate that.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV includes therefore before the final your-sin clause; pinned N1904 has no corresponding οὖν there.
